In 2002, she sold out both Carnegie Hall in New York and the Colosseum in Rome in the same year.

She supported President Raul Alfonsin in the election of 1983 which marked the return of democracy in Argentina following the dictatorship. She referred to this election as "Argentina's Spring" She opposed President Carlos Menem, who was in office from 1989 to 1999, and supported the election of Néstor Kirchner, who became president in 2003.

Sosa received three Latin Grammy nominations for her album, in 2009 . She went on to win Best Folk Album about a month after her death.

'''Haydée Mercedes Sosa''' ({{IPA-es|meɾˌsedes ˈsosa|am}}; 9 July 1935<ref name="birth">[http://www.brainyhistory.com/events/1935/july_9_1935_93941.html Mercedes Sosa] at BrainyHistory.com</ref> – 4 October 2009), sometimes known as '''''La Negra''''' ({{lit|The Black One}}, an affectionate nickname for people with a darker complexion in Argentina), was an Argentine singer who was popular throughout Latin America and many countries outside the region. With her roots in Argentine [[folk music]], Sosa became one of the preeminent exponents of ''El nuevo cancionero''. She gave voice to songs written by many Latin American songwriters. Her music made people hail her as the "voice of the voiceless ones".<ref name="tmc">{{cite web |url=http://www.tmcnet.com/usubmit/2007/12/08/3150199.htm |title=Singer Mercedes Sosa: The voice of the 'voiceless ones' outlasts South American dictatorships}}</ref>

Sosa performed in venues such as the [[Lincoln Center]] in New York City, the [[Théâtre Mogador]] in Paris and the [[Sistine Chapel]] in Vatican City, as well as sell-out shows in New York's [[Carnegie Hall]] and the Roman [[Colosseum]] during her final decade of life. Her career spanned four decades and she was the recipient of six [[Latin Grammy]] awards (2000, 2003, 2004, 2006, 2009, 2011), including a [[Latin Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award]] in 2004 and two posthumous [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Folk Album]] in 2009 and 2011. She won the [[Premios Gardel|Premio Gardel]] in 2000, the main musical award in Argentina. She served as an ambassador for [[UNICEF]].

==Life==
Sosa was born on 9 July 1935, in [[San Miguel de Tucumán]], in the northwestern Argentine province of [[Tucumán Province|Tucumán]], of [[mestizo]] ancestry. She was of French, Spanish and [[Diaguita]] descent.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/> Her parents were [[Peronism|Peronists]], although they never registered in the party, and she started her career as a singer for the Peronist Party in Provincia Tucuman under the name Gladys Osorio.<ref>''Mercedes Sosa: The Voice of Latin America''. Dir. Rodrigo H. Villa. First Run Features, 2013. Web.</ref> In 1950, at age fifteen, she won a singing competition organized by a local radio station and was given a contract to perform for two months.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> She recorded her first album, ''La Voz de la Zafra'', in 1959.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> A performance at the 1965 [[Cosquín Festival|Cosquín National Folklore Festival]]—where she was introduced and brought to the stage while sitting in the audience by fellow folk singer [[Jorge Cafrune]]—<ref name="test">{{YouTube|QzwL8C2hE6c|The presentation by Jorge Cafrune and the song Mercedes Sosa sang}}. Retrieved 3 March 2010.</ref> brought her to the attention of the Argentine public.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary" />

[[File:Mercedes Sosa, Félix Luna y Ariel Ramírez.jpg|left|thumb|Sosa with [[Félix Luna]] and [[Ariel Ramírez]] (at the piano)]]
Sosa and her first husband, Manuel Oscar Matus, with whom she had one son, were key players in the mid-60s ''[[nueva canción]]'' movement (which was called ''nuevo cancionero'' in Argentina).<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> Her second record was ''Canciones con Fundamento'', a collection of Argentine folk songs.

In 1967, Sosa toured the United States and Europe with great success. In later years, she performed and recorded extensively, broadening her repertoire to include material from throughout Latin America.

In the early 1970s, Sosa released two concept albums in collaboration with composer [[Ariel Ramírez]] and lyricist [[Félix Luna]]: ''Cantata Sudamericana'' and ''Mujeres Argentinas'' (Argentine Women). She also recorded a tribute to Chilean musician [[Violeta Parra]] in 1971, including what was to become one of Sosa's signature songs, ''[[Gracias a la Vida]]''.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/><ref name=ap/> She also increased the popularity of songs written by [[Milton Nascimento]] of Brazil and [[Pablo Milanés]] and [[Silvio Rodríguez]] both from [[Cuba]].<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/>

[[File:Mercedes Sosa 2.jpg|thumb|Sosa in 1972]]
After the [[National Reorganization Process|military junta]] of [[Jorge Videla]] came to power in 1976, the atmosphere in Argentina grew increasingly oppressive. Sosa faced death threats against both her and her family, but refused for many years to leave the country. At a concert in [[La Plata]] in 1979, Sosa was searched and arrested on stage, along with all those attending the concert.<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> Their release came about through international intervention.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> Banned in her own country, she moved to Paris and then to [[Madrid]].<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/><ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/>

Sosa returned to Argentina from her exile in Europe in 1982,<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> several months before the military regime collapsed as a result of the [[Falklands War]], and gave a series of concerts at the ''[[Teatro Opera|Teatro Ópera]]'' in Buenos Aires, where she invited many of her younger colleagues to share the stage. A double album of recordings from these performances became an instant best seller. In subsequent years, Sosa continued to tour both in Argentina and abroad, performing in such venues as the [[Lincoln Center]] in New York City and the ''[[Théâtre Mogador]]'' in Paris. By then, she was already called America's voice. In poor health for much of the 1990s, she performed a comeback show in Argentina in 1998.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> In 1994, she played the [[Sistine Chapel]] in Vatican City.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite web |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20091004-legendary-folk-singer-mercedes-sosa-dies-74-argentina-entertainment-music |title=Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74 |date=4 October 2009 |access-date=5 October 2009 |publisher=[[France 24]]}}</ref> In 2002, she sold out both [[Carnegie Hall]] in New York and the [[Colosseum]] in Rome in the same year.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/>

[[File:Mercedes Sosa.jpg|thumb|left|Sosa in 1973]]
A supporter of [[Juan Perón|Perón]], she favored leftist causes throughout her life. She opposed President [[Carlos Menem]], who was in office from 1989 to 1999, and supported the election of [[Néstor Kirchner]], who became president in 2003.<ref>[http://www.berlinonline.de/berliner-zeitung/archiv/.bin/dump.fcgi/2003/1025/magazin/0001/ Interview with Mercedes Sosa] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016201953/http://www.berlinonline.de/berliner-zeitung/archiv/.bin/dump.fcgi/2003/1025/magazin/0001/ |date=16 October 2009 }}, ''Magazin Berliner Zeitung'', 25 October 2003. {{in lang|de}}</ref>
Sosa was a [[UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador]] for Latin America and the Caribbean.<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/><ref>[http://chicago.cervantes.es/Cultura/Fichas/Ficha41728_47_2.htm Mercedes Sosa in concert] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080104200631/http://chicago.cervantes.es/Cultura/Fichas/Ficha41728_47_2.htm |date=4 January 2008 }}</ref>

In a career spanning four decades, she worked with performers across several genres and generations, folk, opera, pop, rock, including [[Martha Argerich]], [[Andrea Bocelli]], [[David Broza]], [[Franco Battiato]], [[Jaime Roos]], [[Joan Baez]], [[Francis Cabrel]], [[Gal Costa]], [[Luz Casal]], [[Lila Downs]], [[Lucio Dalla]], [[Maria Farantouri]], [[Lucecita Benitez]], [[Nilda Fernández]], [[Charly Garcia]], [[León Gieco]], [[Gian Marco]], [[Nana Mouskouri]], [[Pablo Milanés]], [[Holly Near]], [[Milton Nascimento]], [[Pata Negra]], [[Fito Páez]], [[Franco De Vita]], [[Lourdes Pérez]], [[Luciano Pavarotti]], [[Silvio Rodríguez]], [[Ismael Serrano]], [[Shakira]], [[Sting (musician)|Sting]], [[Caetano Veloso]],<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/> [[Julieta Venegas]], [[Gustavo Cerati]] and [[Konstantin Wecker]]<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies">{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/8289370.stm |title=Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies |date=4 October 2009 |access-date=5 October 2009 |publisher=[[BBC]]}}</ref>

Sosa participated in a 1999 production of [[Ariel Ramírez]]'s ''Misa Criolla''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://soundsandcolours.com/articles/argentina/in-profile-mercedes-sosa-1761/ |title=In Profile: Mercedes Sosa |website=soundsandcolours.com |date=26 August 2010 |access-date=27 March 2018}}</ref> Her song ''Balderrama'' is featured in the 2008 movie ''[[Che (2008 film)|Che]]'', starring [[Benicio del Toro]] as the Argentine [[Marxist]] revolutionary [[Che Guevara]].<ref>{{YouTube|k4LJDTlviKw|''Balderrama'' by Mercedes Sosa}} – a tribute to [[Che Guevara]]</ref>

Sosa was the former co-chair of the [[Earth Charter]] International Commission.

==Awards==
She won the Latin Grammy Award for Best Folk Album in 2000 (''Misa Criolla''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2000) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2000&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2003 (''Acústico''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2003) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2003&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2006 (''Corazón Libre''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2006) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2006&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2009 (''[[Cantora, un Viaje Íntimo|Cantora 1]]'', which also won [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Recording Package|Best Recording Package]] and was nominated for [[Latin Grammy Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]]),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2009) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2009&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> and 2011 (''Deja La Vida Volar''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2011) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2011&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> as well as several international awards.

In 1995, [[Konex Foundation]] from Argentina granted her the Diamond [[Konex Award]], one of the most prestigious awards in Argentina, as the most important personality in the Popular Music of her country in the last decade.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premios Konex 1995: Música Popular |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/premios1995-musica-popular |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Fundación Konex |language=es}}</ref>

==Death==
[[File:Funeral de Mercedes Sosa.jpg|thumb|Mercedes Sosa lying in repose, with her family and President [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]] viewing]]
Suffering from recurrent endocrine and respiratory problems in later years, the 74-year-old Sosa was hospitalized in Buenos Aires on 18 September 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clarin.com/diario/2009/10/01/um/m-02010016.htm|title="En ningún momento sufrió", dijo el hijo de Mercedes Sosa|date=October 2009}}</ref> She died from [[multiple organ failure]] on 4 October 2009, at 5:15 am.<ref name=ap>[https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5iBSb5ZdEJ8MI6_qzWccZNZQITnMAD9B47Q8G1 Associated Press]{{dead link|date=July 2012}}</ref> She is survived by one son, Fabián Matus, born of her first marriage.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/><ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74"/> He said: "She lived her 74 years to the fullest. She had done practically everything she wanted, she didn't have any type of barrier or any type of fear that limited her".<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74">{{cite web|author=Javier Doberti|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2009/SHOWBIZ/Music/10/04/obit.mercedes.sosa/|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref> The hospital expressed its sympathies to her relatives.<ref name="Argentine folk legend Mercedes Sosa dead at 74">{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/news/world/156066/argentine-folk-legend-mercedes-sosa-dead-at-74|title=Argentine folk legend Mercedes Sosa dead at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|newspaper=[[Bangkok Post]]}}</ref> Her website featured the following: "Her undisputed talent, her honesty and her profound convictions leave a great legacy to future generations".<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74"/>

Her body was placed on display at the [[Argentine National Congress|National Congress]] building in Buenos Aires for the public to pay their respects, and President Fernández de Kirchner ordered three days of national mourning.<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/nota.asp?nota_id=1182377&pid=7460859&toi=6255|title=Continúa la procesión en el Congreso para despedir a Mercedes Sosa}}</ref> Thousands had queued by the end of the day.<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2009/10/200910421057755554.html#|title=Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref> She was cremated on 5 October.<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2009/10/200910421057755554.html#|title=Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref><ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|author=Helen Popper|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/hollywood/idINTRE5931S220091004|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

Sosa's obituary in ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' said she was "an unrivalled interpreter of works by her compatriot, the Argentine [[Atahualpa Yupanqui]], and Chile's [[Violeta Parra]]".<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/culture-obituaries/music-obituaries/6259898/Mercedes-Sosa.html|title=Mercedes Sosa: Obituary|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref> Helen Popper of [[Reuters]] reported her death by saying she "fought South America's dictators with her voice and became a giant of contemporary Latin American music".<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|author=Helen Popper|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/hollywood/idINTRE5931S220091004|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Sosa received three [[Latin Grammy]] nominations for her album, in 2009 . She went on to win Best Folk Album about a month after her death.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/><ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/>

==Tribute==
In 2019, she was celebrated by a [[Google Doodle]]. The doodle was showcased in [[Argentina]], Chile, [[Uruguay]], [[Paraguay]], [[Bolivia]], [[Peru]], [[Ecuador]], [[Cuba]], [[Iceland]], Sweden, [[Serbia]], [[Greece]], [[Israel]] and [[Vietnam]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.google.com/doodles/celebrating-mercedes-sosa|title=Celebrating Mercedes Sosa|work=Doodles Archive, Google|date=31 January 2019}}</ref>

'''Haydée Mercedes Sosa''' ({{IPA-es|meɾˌsedes ˈsosa|am}}; 9 July 1935<ref name="birth">[http://www.brainyhistory.com/events/1935/july_9_1935_93941.html Mercedes Sosa] at BrainyHistory.com</ref> – 4 October 2009), sometimes known as '''''La Negra''''' ({{lit|The Black One}}, an affectionate nickname for people with a darker complexion in Argentina), was an Argentine singer who was popular throughout Latin America and many countries outside the region. With her roots in Argentine [[folk music]], Sosa became one of the preeminent exponents of ''El nuevo cancionero''. She gave voice to songs written by many Latin American songwriters. Her music made people hail her as the "voice of the voiceless ones".<ref name="tmc">{{cite web |url=http://www.tmcnet.com/usubmit/2007/12/08/3150199.htm |title=Singer Mercedes Sosa: The voice of the 'voiceless ones' outlasts South American dictatorships}}</ref>

Sosa performed in venues such as the [[Lincoln Center]] in New York City, the [[Théâtre Mogador]] in Paris and the [[Sistine Chapel]] in Vatican City, as well as sell-out shows in New York's [[Carnegie Hall]] and the Roman [[Colosseum]] during her final decade of life. Her career spanned four decades and she was the recipient of six [[Latin Grammy]] awards (2000, 2003, 2004, 2006, 2009, 2011), including a [[Latin Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award]] in 2004 and two posthumous [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Folk Album]] in 2009 and 2011. She won the [[Premios Gardel|Premio Gardel]] in 2000, the main musical award in Argentina. She served as an ambassador for [[UNICEF]].

==Life==
Sosa was born on 9 July 1935, in [[San Miguel de Tucumán]], in the northwestern Argentine province of [[Tucumán Province|Tucumán]], of [[mestizo]] ancestry. She was of French, Spanish and [[Diaguita]] descent.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/> Her parents were [[Peronism|Peronists]], although they never registered in the party, and she started her career as a singer for the Peronist Party in Provincia Tucuman under the name Gladys Osorio.<ref>''Mercedes Sosa: The Voice of Latin America''. Dir. Rodrigo H. Villa. First Run Features, 2013. Web.</ref> In 1950, at age fifteen, she won a singing competition organized by a local radio station and was given a contract to perform for two months.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> She recorded her first album, ''La Voz de la Zafra'', in 1959.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> A performance at the 1965 [[Cosquín Festival|Cosquín National Folklore Festival]]—where she was introduced and brought to the stage while sitting in the audience by fellow folk singer [[Jorge Cafrune]]—<ref name="test">{{YouTube|QzwL8C2hE6c|The presentation by Jorge Cafrune and the song Mercedes Sosa sang}}. Retrieved 3 March 2010.</ref> brought her to the attention of the Argentine public.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary" />

[[File:Mercedes Sosa, Félix Luna y Ariel Ramírez.jpg|left|thumb|Sosa with [[Félix Luna]] and [[Ariel Ramírez]] (at the piano)]]
Sosa and her first husband, Manuel Oscar Matus, with whom she had one son, were key players in the mid-60s ''[[nueva canción]]'' movement (which was called ''nuevo cancionero'' in Argentina).<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> Her second record was ''Canciones con Fundamento'', a collection of Argentine folk songs.

In 1967, Sosa toured the United States and Europe with great success. In later years, she performed and recorded extensively, broadening her repertoire to include material from throughout Latin America.

In the early 1970s, Sosa released two concept albums in collaboration with composer [[Ariel Ramírez]] and lyricist [[Félix Luna]]: ''Cantata Sudamericana'' and ''Mujeres Argentinas'' (Argentine Women). She also recorded a tribute to Chilean musician [[Violeta Parra]] in 1971, including what was to become one of Sosa's signature songs, ''[[Gracias a la Vida]]''.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/><ref name=ap/> She also increased the popularity of songs written by [[Milton Nascimento]] of Brazil and [[Pablo Milanés]] and [[Silvio Rodríguez]] both from [[Cuba]].<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/>

[[File:Mercedes Sosa 2.jpg|thumb|Sosa in 1972]]
After the [[National Reorganization Process|military junta]] of [[Jorge Videla]] came to power in 1976, the atmosphere in Argentina grew increasingly oppressive. Sosa faced death threats against both her and her family, but refused for many years to leave the country. At a concert in [[La Plata]] in 1979, Sosa was searched and arrested on stage, along with all those attending the concert.<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> Their release came about through international intervention.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> Banned in her own country, she moved to Paris and then to [[Madrid]].<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/><ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/>

Sosa returned to Argentina from her exile in Europe in 1982,<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/> several months before the military regime collapsed as a result of the [[Falklands War]], and gave a series of concerts at the ''[[Teatro Opera|Teatro Ópera]]'' in Buenos Aires, where she invited many of her younger colleagues to share the stage. A double album of recordings from these performances became an instant best seller. In subsequent years, Sosa continued to tour both in Argentina and abroad, performing in such venues as the [[Lincoln Center]] in New York City and the ''[[Théâtre Mogador]]'' in Paris. By then, she was already called America's voice. In poor health for much of the 1990s, she performed a comeback show in Argentina in 1998.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/> In 1994, she played the [[Sistine Chapel]] in Vatican City.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite web |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20091004-legendary-folk-singer-mercedes-sosa-dies-74-argentina-entertainment-music |title=Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74 |date=4 October 2009 |access-date=5 October 2009 |publisher=[[France 24]]}}</ref> In 2002, she sold out both [[Carnegie Hall]] in New York and the [[Colosseum]] in Rome in the same year.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/>

[[File:Mercedes Sosa.jpg|thumb|left|Sosa in 1973]]
A supporter of [[Juan Perón|Perón]], she favored leftist causes throughout her life. She opposed President [[Carlos Menem]], who was in office from 1989 to 1999, and supported the election of [[Néstor Kirchner]], who became president in 2003.<ref>[http://www.berlinonline.de/berliner-zeitung/archiv/.bin/dump.fcgi/2003/1025/magazin/0001/ Interview with Mercedes Sosa] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016201953/http://www.berlinonline.de/berliner-zeitung/archiv/.bin/dump.fcgi/2003/1025/magazin/0001/ |date=16 October 2009 }}, ''Magazin Berliner Zeitung'', 25 October 2003. {{in lang|de}}</ref>
Sosa was a [[UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador]] for Latin America and the Caribbean.<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/><ref>[http://chicago.cervantes.es/Cultura/Fichas/Ficha41728_47_2.htm Mercedes Sosa in concert] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080104200631/http://chicago.cervantes.es/Cultura/Fichas/Ficha41728_47_2.htm |date=4 January 2008 }}</ref>

In a career spanning four decades, she worked with performers across several genres and generations, folk, opera, pop, rock, including [[Martha Argerich]], [[Andrea Bocelli]], [[David Broza]], [[Franco Battiato]], [[Jaime Roos]], [[Joan Baez]], [[Francis Cabrel]], [[Gal Costa]], [[Luz Casal]], [[Lila Downs]], [[Lucio Dalla]], [[Maria Farantouri]], [[Lucecita Benitez]], [[Nilda Fernández]], [[Charly Garcia]], [[León Gieco]], [[Gian Marco]], [[Nana Mouskouri]], [[Pablo Milanés]], [[Holly Near]], [[Milton Nascimento]], [[Pata Negra]], [[Fito Páez]], [[Franco De Vita]], [[Lourdes Pérez]], [[Luciano Pavarotti]], [[Silvio Rodríguez]], [[Ismael Serrano]], [[Shakira]], [[Sting (musician)|Sting]], [[Caetano Veloso]],<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/> [[Julieta Venegas]], [[Gustavo Cerati]] and [[Konstantin Wecker]]<ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies">{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/8289370.stm |title=Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies |date=4 October 2009 |access-date=5 October 2009 |publisher=[[BBC]]}}</ref>

Sosa participated in a 1999 production of [[Ariel Ramírez]]'s ''Misa Criolla''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://soundsandcolours.com/articles/argentina/in-profile-mercedes-sosa-1761/ |title=In Profile: Mercedes Sosa |website=soundsandcolours.com |date=26 August 2010 |access-date=27 March 2018}}</ref> Her song ''Balderrama'' is featured in the 2008 movie ''[[Che (2008 film)|Che]]'', starring [[Benicio del Toro]] as the Argentine [[Marxist]] revolutionary [[Che Guevara]].<ref>{{YouTube|k4LJDTlviKw|''Balderrama'' by Mercedes Sosa}} – a tribute to [[Che Guevara]]</ref>

Sosa was the former co-chair of the [[Earth Charter]] International Commission.

==Awards==
She won the Latin Grammy Award for Best Folk Album in 2000 (''Misa Criolla''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2000) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2000&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2003 (''Acústico''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2003) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2003&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2006 (''Corazón Libre''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2006) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2006&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> 2009 (''[[Cantora, un Viaje Íntimo|Cantora 1]]'', which also won [[Latin Grammy Award for Best Recording Package|Best Recording Package]] and was nominated for [[Latin Grammy Award for Album of the Year|Album of the Year]]),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2009) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2009&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> and 2011 (''Deja La Vida Volar''),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Latin Grammys: Ganadores – Años Anteriores (2011) |url=https://www.latingrammy.com/es/nominees/search?artist=&field_nominee_work_value=&year=2011&genre=All |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Latin Grammys |publisher=The Latin Recording Academy |language=es}}</ref> as well as several international awards.

In 1995, [[Konex Foundation]] from Argentina granted her the Diamond [[Konex Award]], one of the most prestigious awards in Argentina, as the most important personality in the Popular Music of her country in the last decade.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Premios Konex 1995: Música Popular |url=https://www.fundacionkonex.org/premios1995-musica-popular |access-date=7 July 2021 |website=Fundación Konex |language=es}}</ref>

==Death==
[[File:Funeral de Mercedes Sosa.jpg|thumb|Mercedes Sosa lying in repose, with her family and President [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]] viewing]]
Suffering from recurrent endocrine and respiratory problems in later years, the 74-year-old Sosa was hospitalized in Buenos Aires on 18 September 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clarin.com/diario/2009/10/01/um/m-02010016.htm|title="En ningún momento sufrió", dijo el hijo de Mercedes Sosa|date=October 2009}}</ref> She died from [[multiple organ failure]] on 4 October 2009, at 5:15 am.<ref name=ap>[https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5iBSb5ZdEJ8MI6_qzWccZNZQITnMAD9B47Q8G1 Associated Press]{{dead link|date=July 2012}}</ref> She is survived by one son, Fabián Matus, born of her first marriage.<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary"/><ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74"/> He said: "She lived her 74 years to the fullest. She had done practically everything she wanted, she didn't have any type of barrier or any type of fear that limited her".<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74">{{cite web|author=Javier Doberti|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2009/SHOWBIZ/Music/10/04/obit.mercedes.sosa/|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[CNN]]}}</ref> The hospital expressed its sympathies to her relatives.<ref name="Argentine folk legend Mercedes Sosa dead at 74">{{cite news|url=http://www.bangkokpost.com/news/world/156066/argentine-folk-legend-mercedes-sosa-dead-at-74|title=Argentine folk legend Mercedes Sosa dead at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|newspaper=[[Bangkok Post]]}}</ref> Her website featured the following: "Her undisputed talent, her honesty and her profound convictions leave a great legacy to future generations".<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74"/>

Her body was placed on display at the [[Argentine National Congress|National Congress]] building in Buenos Aires for the public to pay their respects, and President Fernández de Kirchner ordered three days of national mourning.<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa, 'voice of Latin America,' dies at 74"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/nota.asp?nota_id=1182377&pid=7460859&toi=6255|title=Continúa la procesión en el Congreso para despedir a Mercedes Sosa}}</ref> Thousands had queued by the end of the day.<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2009/10/200910421057755554.html#|title=Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref> She was cremated on 5 October.<ref name="Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/news/americas/2009/10/200910421057755554.html#|title=Argentine folk icon Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|publisher=[[Al Jazeera]]}}</ref><ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|author=Helen Popper|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/hollywood/idINTRE5931S220091004|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

Sosa's obituary in ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'' said she was "an unrivalled interpreter of works by her compatriot, the Argentine [[Atahualpa Yupanqui]], and Chile's [[Violeta Parra]]".<ref name="Mercedes Sosa: Obituary">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/culture-obituaries/music-obituaries/6259898/Mercedes-Sosa.html|title=Mercedes Sosa: Obituary|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]}}</ref> Helen Popper of [[Reuters]] reported her death by saying she "fought South America's dictators with her voice and became a giant of contemporary Latin American music".<ref name="Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74">{{cite news|author=Helen Popper|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/hollywood/idINTRE5931S220091004|title=Argentine singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74|date=4 October 2009|access-date=5 October 2009|work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> Sosa received three [[Latin Grammy]] nominations for her album, in 2009 . She went on to win Best Folk Album about a month after her death.<ref name="Legendary folk singer Mercedes Sosa dies at 74"/><ref name="Latin artist Mercedes Sosa dies"/>
